assessment.rationale: Held: giving schools and clinics water, toilets and soap is a known, costed answer, not an unsolved research problem. The interventions are standard WASH infrastructure, and WHO and UNICEF publish the open WASH FIT improvement tool for health facilities, a 2025 global implementation report (https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240104822) and school operation and maintenance costing tools; WHO and UNICEF estimate universal basic WASH in health facilities in the 46 least developed countries at US$6.5 to 9.6 billion over ten years, about US$0.65 per capita per year, and call it highly cost-effective (https://washinhcf.org/latest_news/full-analysis-of-global-costs-for-providing-basic-wash-services-in-hcf/). Honest limit: the 2,000,000-facility KPI is unmet. The 2026 JMP school report estimates that in 2025, 429 million school-age children lacked basic drinking water at school, 460 million basic sanitation and 545 million basic hygiene (https://data.unicef.org/resources/jmp-wash-in-schools-2026/), and the 2026 health-facility update reports only 40 percent of facilities with basic sanitation and 2.3 billion people without basic hygiene at their facility (https://washdata.org/node/29). Those are financing, delivery and maintenance gaps with known answers, so under the 29 September 2026 rule the project is not opened as new work. A reframed project on a specific unsolved technical gap, such as verifying sustained functionality at low cost, would need its own prior-art basis.

additionalSearches.query: JMP 2024 WASH in schools health care facilities lacking basic water sanitation hygiene services billion
additionalSearches.finding: JMP 2024 health-facility report: 78 percent of facilities had basic water and 57 percent basic hygiene in 2022. The 2026 update (2025 data): basic water at 85 percent of facilities (1.2 billion people without), basic sanitation at 40 percent, basic hygiene at 72 percent (2.3 billion without), 3.4 billion without basic waste management.

additionalSearches.query: WASH FIT health care facilities tool WHO UNICEF schools WASH package proven cost per facility
additionalSearches.finding: WASH FIT is the WHO/UNICEF risk-based improvement tool covering water, sanitation, hand hygiene, cleaning and waste for small facilities in low- and middle-income countries, with a February 2025 global implementation report; universal basic WASH in HCF in 46 LDCs is costed at US$6.5 to 9.6 billion over 10 years (about US$0.65 per capita per year). No per-facility cost published.

additionalSearches.query: JMP 2024 WASH in schools report children without basic drinking water sanitation hygiene service at school
additionalSearches.finding: JMP 2024 schools report: 447 million children lacked basic drinking water, 427 million basic sanitation and 646 million basic hygiene at school (2023). The 2026 edition (2025 data): 429 million lacked basic drinking water, 460 million basic sanitation and 545 million basic hygiene.

additionalSearches.query: health care facilities WASH universal access 2030 cost-effective interventions known solutions financing gap UNICEF WHO 2026 report
additionalSearches.finding: The 2025 WHO/UNICEF Global Progress Report on WASH, Waste and Electricity in HCF: about 1.1 billion people treated in facilities without clean water in 2023; universal basic WASH in LDC facilities achievable for under US$10 billion and described as highly cost-effective; recommends costed national road maps and health-budget integration. Financing, not technology, is the gap.
